analysis:
The supplied changes are test-only. NativeToolStreamRouterTests.swift (head lines 413-479) updates the legacy forced-mode expectation: ASCII framing whitespace (space, tab, CR, LF) is now dropped, while prose and other Unicode whitespace (VT, FF, NEL, NBSP, ZWSP, LS, U+3000, BOM) still raise toolChoiceViolation. The new test covers the legacy, native and MiMo paths at every scalar chunking width. It also checks that auto mode streams the same bytes unchanged. StructuredForcedToolAdmissionTests.swift is a new file, but only its metadata and a truncated patch excerpt were supplied, so I could not examine its body. It appears to qualify catalog builds for required or named tool_choice, which is serving-contract testing rather than a security control.

No production source was supplied. The router implementation that actually drops framing whitespace sits in a changed or unchanged file outside this batch, so the behavior change is only inferred from the test expectations. The related threats are T-007/T-056: forced tool_choice output integrity, and the fact that attestation does not prove correct computation. Dropping ASCII whitespace only, before a validated call, does not expose plaintext, authorization or key material. It does not touch TB-002, TB-009 or TB-011. The tests assert that prose fail-closed behavior is preserved, so I found no regression or threat-model gap in the supplied evidence.

The next pass should check the production router change for the following: that whitespace is dropped only before any visible content; that bounded buffering has no unbounded-whitespace DoS (an endless stream of whitespace in forced mode); and that the admitted-builds list matches the catalog and parser resolution.
